sentences.text: Akanthosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilians known as the "spine crocodile" due to its dermal armor.
The armor of Akanthosuchus was unusual for having elongate spikes or broad blades.
The spikes on the armor rose up to 29.0 mm, nearly as tall as the base of the scutes they sat on.
Akanthosuchus is unique among known crocodilians for possessing both spiked and bladed scutes.
Analysis of growth rings suggests the type specimen was at least eight years old when it died.
The genus Akanthosuchus was described by F. Michael O'Neill and colleagues in 1981.
The type species A. langstoni was named in honor of paleontologist Wann Langston Jr.
Fossils of Akanthosuchus are found in the Paleocene-aged Nacimiento Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.
The tail may have been relatively short, indicated by the reduction of bony projections on the tail vertebrae.
The thigh bone of the type specimen was 137 mm long, while the shin bone was 102 mm long.
Akanthosuchus belongs to the parent group Alligatoroidea.
O'Neill and colleagues suggested Akanthosuchus was an alligatorine based on characteristics of a partial lower jaw bone.
Hill and Lucas later used cladistic analysis to reject the idea that Akanthosuchus is the same as Ceratosuchus or Navajosuchus, finding it to be an alligatoroid.
The time range for Akanthosuchus is the Danian to Selandian stages, from 66 to 60.9 million years ago.
Later research confirmed Akanthosuchus langstoni existed in the older Puercan-age portion of the Nacimiento Formation.
It is debated whether Akanthosuchus is strongly an alligatorine, as Hill and Lucas found this classification to be weakly supported.
